newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Thursday were quiet, with no sales reported following this week's active trade, feedlot sources said.

Most showlists in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area were sold as were most of the showlists in Kansas, sources in the respective areas said. Cattle sold at a top of $66.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from last week.
Most of the remaining cattle were 'green' or unfinished and priced at $66.00, but no bids were reported, sources said.
About 75,000 head sold in the Panhandle this week and about 87,000 in Kansas.
Feedlot cattle strength also was tied to active beef sales on Wednesday at slightly higher prices. Beef Wednesday was quoted up $0.22 to $0.55 per cwt on 389 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.

Lighter slaughter rates and lighter-weight cattle, compared with a year ago, were producing less beef, which supported beef prices and underpinned fed cattle prices, said Andy Gottschalk, livestock analyst with LFG.
"That weight differential is being compounded now by the adverse weather," Gottschalk said.
